page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-48GB is a Cloud Native family virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 8 shared vCPUs operating at 2.0 GHz. The system is configured with 48.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this server type, and there are no hardware GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate a balanced profile with some notable tradeoffs. While the Geekbench single-core score is strong, the stress-ng single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 10%. Multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests consistently ranks in the average range. Memory bandwidth presents a bottleneck for larger datasets, with uncached read and write speeds for 256MB blocks categorized as weak, though cached small-block reads remain average.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this server is positioned as a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU threads. It is well-suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, Redis caching, and database operations, all of which demonstrated average benchmark throughput. It is less suitable for memory-intensive large-block processing or medium-to-large language model inference due to degraded performance in those areas.
